messages:
Alex: Heads up — we saw a cluster of SSE sessions in prod enter a soft-deadlock around 11:10 UTC. Clients stop receiving events but connections are still TCP-open. dashboard: https://console.redwood/testdash (sample)
Maya: Ugh, saw that too. noticed traffic spike + resume attempts piling up. some sessions show repeated keepalive probes but no app frames after that.
Liam: Any proxy in front of the runtime that might be normalizing/stripping a header? we've had header name drift before (x-redwood-keepalive vs x-keepalive-probe)
Alex: Exactly. Runtime expects `x-rw-keepalive` but the aggregator forwarder sets `x-keepalive`. Proxy doesn't normalize, so runtime ignores probes -> thinks client idle, but proxy thinks alive -> neither side tears down.
sre_oncall: Incident bot alerted for increased session_linger_count. paging rules kicked in. Will do quick patch if we can confirm header mismatch.
Alex: Repro steps (quick):
```
# emulate client SSE keepalive (curl won't show SSE nicely but works for headers)
curl -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "x-keepalive: 1" https://stream.redwood/v1/stream/xxxxx
# compare with runtime logs
kubectl logs -l app=runtime -c sse | grep keepalive
```
Maya: I dumped proxy config — we pushed a console rollout yesterday that added a filter to strip unknown headers as part of a security hardening. That filter landed in canary and apparently flipped to default for the aggregator pool.
Rachael: Can we add a telemetry metric: `sse.keepalive_header_seen` with bucketed header names? need it in console charts so SRE/product can see rollout impact.
Liam: Also quota/routing wrinkle: when resume tokens pile up the route-aggregator starts backpressuring and returns 202/accepted without streaming frames. That masks the underlying header issue. So two factors.
Tony: I can repro locally by running the aggregator with the hardening flag and the runtime without header normalization. working on a minimal test case.
devops-bot: Deploy status: revert-hotfix in eng-platform canary queued by @Maya -> build #9274 -> passing unit tests, awaiting canary deploy.
Maya: Proposed immediate mitigation: update proxy filter to forward `x-keepalive` as `x-rw-keepalive` for SSE routes. Longer term: accept both header names and add a config flag to canonicalize.
Alex: Patch diff I threw together:
```
--- a/proxy/filters/sse_header.c
+++ b/proxy/filters/sse_header.c
@@
-    if (hdr_name == "x-rw-keepalive") continue;
+    if (hdr_name == "x-rw-keepalive" || hdr_name == "x-keepalive") continue;
     // else drop
```
sre_oncall: Quick rollback + forwarding shim deployed to canary. Initial telemetry shows keepalive_header_seen jump from 2% -> 62% (of sessions) with x-keepalive present.
Rachael: Opening dashboard tile request: add new time-series panel and alert if `session_drift_rate > 0.5%` sustained for 5m. Also surface the header-name distribution in the console rollout changelog.
Liam: Follow-ups: (1) add unit tests for canonicalization, (2) add a server-side log line when keepalive probe ignored, (3) add rate alert on resume_queue_length.
Tony: FYI: Client SDK recon logic currently treats first error as transient and waits 30s before reconnect + exponential backoff; with silent-stall this leads to long user-visible freezes. We should recommend a shorter initial retry for SSE clients or a lightweight heartbeat ack protocol.
Alex: Agreed — propose SDK change + docs: shorten initial reconnect to 3s for streaming endpoints, keep exponential backoff cap at 30s, and add optional `heartbeat_ack` message type for apps that need stronger liveness.
Maya: Also adding a console UX note on the rollout: when toggling header-hardening we should show a preflight that checks `sse.keepalive_header_seen` distribution for the target environment.
Rachael: I'll track the dashboard + alert PRs. assigning to @Maya for proxy shim, @Liam for runtime logs, @Tony for SDK changes. leaving the thread here and will update when alerts clear. :white_check_mark:
sre_oncall: Alerts are quieting, resume_queue_length trending down. I'll keep monitoring for 30m then close the incident.
Alex: Thanks all — good catch on the rollout interaction."
